summary.headline: FY26 revenue hit a record INR375 crore (+56% YoY) and Q4 revenue INR113.8 crore (+78% YoY), with PAT up 92% to INR46.9 crore.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a recovery year, with revenue of INR375 crore, EBITDA of INR92 crore (24.6% margin) and PAT of INR46.9 crore (12.5% margin). Q4 FY26 was the highest quarter in company history at INR113.8 crore revenue, 18% above Q3, with EBITDA of INR27.8 crore and PAT of INR15.5 crore. Growth came mainly from Transfer Cases (+66%) and Components (+124%, export-led), while EV transmissions grew only 10%. The company is debt-free and proposed a final dividend of INR3.27 per share.

financial_highlights.change: +56% YoY from INR240 crore in FY25
+189% YoY from INR5.4 crore; +32% QoQ from INR11.8 crore
From around 6% earlier; crossed 20% in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR3.27 per equity share (face value INR5)

segments.name: Transfer Case
segments.commentary: Revenue up 66% in FY26; volumes about 52,000 units vs low-30,000s in FY25 (roughly 70-80% growth). Primary growth driver, with Indonesia export orders for Mahindra Scorpio pickup and Tata Yodha pickup.

segments.name: EV transmission
segments.commentary: Revenue up 10% in FY26, range-bound on subdued EV volumes. About 24,000 units; capacity utilisation around 25-30%. A delayed new 90-120 kW model is expected to double EV volumes from July 2026.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: Revenue up 124% in FY26, export-led, with customers including BorgWarner and Magna. Over 13 lakh parts shipped; monthly run rate up from about INR7 crore to INR10-12 crore.

segments.name: Manual transmission and synchronizers
segments.commentary: Revenue nearly doubled in FY26 from a small base. Pursuing a full manual transmission programme with a leading Indian OEM, with volumes potentially up to 100,000 a year.

segments.name: Automatic transmission
segments.commentary: No revenue yet. Company is in advanced talks on a technology transfer agreement with a global OEM and is completing due diligence; proof-of-concept targeted within about one quarter.

guidance_outlook: Expects momentum in Transfer Cases and Components to continue into coming quarters; EV volumes to ramp from the new model going into production by July 2026.
Indonesia Transfer Case orders (about 70,000 units, split between Tata and Mahindra) are on track for completion in FY27.
Medium-term export contribution target of 20-25% of revenue.
Newly secured component programmes expected to add annual revenue near INR100 crore, with volumes above 1 million parts a year.

Management indicated an automatic transmission opportunity of about INR1,000 crore in its guidance, deliberately conservative (volume basis 80,000-100,000 units a year); a 4-wheel drive global business potential of around INR300 crore was called out.
Expects to maintain a healthy net cash position despite expansion and working capital needs.
capex_capacity: EV transmission capacity utilisation is about 25-30%; management says better utilisation will improve financial efficiency.
US wholly owned subsidiary approved by the Board; initial outlay about INR3 crore for offices, infrastructure and a small warehouse, with two experienced staff on the ground by July-August 2026.
Manual transmission line is being designed to handle a low-volume and a high-volume model (60,000-100,000 units a year).
Three DCT (dual-clutch) projects in development with two customers; first trickle revenue expected mid-to-second half of calendar 2027, with larger volumes a year later.
Next-generation Torque-on-Demand Transfer Case with M-Lock technology developed with Mahindra; discussions underway for production integration.
Japanese OEM transfer case nomination with SOP in FY28-29; prototype and proof-of-concept already completed.
demand_pricing: Transfer Case demand supported by 4-wheel drive adoption, new launches and new Tata Sierra 4WD contract; US Ford application volume uplift at a Tier 1 customer.
Indonesia tender won against at least 3-4 Japanese OEMs and two large Chinese companies; order split equally between Tata and Mahindra.
Management says the Indonesia order is on track despite media reports of a government hold, and that the work is serious.
EV market is highly competitive (Mahindra's Tier 1, MG Windsor); management sees a decisive edge in some programmes.
Exports rising, helped by rupee depreciation and possible India-US and India-EU trade deals.
Components growth is said to be driven by engineering solutions, quality and right-first-time delivery, not only cost.

qa_highlights.question: What were the volumes for Transfer Case, EV transmission and Components, and what is EV capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Transfer Case volume about 52,000 (from low-30,000s); E-gear drive about 24,000; Components over 13 lakh parts. EV utilisation about 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Indonesia order on track for FY27, and what drives revenue in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track for FY27. Other drivers cited: Tata Sierra 4WD, US Ford uplift, Mahindra global pickup support in South Africa, EV designs and 3-wheeler prototypes with two customers, and a truck manual transmission opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Will the US investment (about INR3 crore) cover components only or also proprietary products?
qa_highlights.answer: The US is a beachhead for market understanding, programme management and expos, covering transfer cases and proprietary products as well as components. The INR3 crore covers offices and a small warehouse. Pricing and margins in the US may be the best.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company pursue inorganic growth in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers organic growth given the size of the business and the cultural adaptation required.

qa_highlights.question: Indonesia order status: is it on hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management dismissed the media reports as frivolous. It says the tender was won fairly, the order must be executed before 31 March 2027, and the Japanese and Chinese bidders were not ready.

qa_highlights.question: How much EV volume and capacity is coming, and how competitive is the segment?
qa_highlights.answer: New 90-120 kW design across Nexon, Curvv, Punch higher trim and Harrier front axle has completed Tata testing with production approval; volumes expected in FY27. Management is also exploring China with a sales representative, and the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: How did the INR1,500-plus crore potential annual revenue become INR2,000-plus crore, and which segment adds INR500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Automatic transmission is the cornerstone. A 200,000-unit global 4WD business would be about INR800 crore, but guidance carries about INR300 crore for 4WD. Automatic transmission figure assumes 80,000-100,000 units a year, and total estimate is about INR1,000 crore, deliberately conservative.

risks_watch: Indonesia orders (about 70,000 units) must be delivered by March 2027; media reports of a government hold were disputed by management.
FY28 revenue visibility depends on converting the DCT, 3-wheeler, manual transmission and automatic transmission programmes, most of which are still at prototype or negotiation stage.
EV volumes depend on the delayed Tata model going into production by July 2026; EV utilisation is only 25-30%.
Automatic transmission technology transfer agreement is still in negotiation; the due diligence and proof-of-concept are pending.
Brand perception of Indian suppliers and competition (Japanese, Chinese, multinational Tier 1s) could affect global wins.
US subsidiary economics are unproven; initial spend is small but the business model is still being designed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, especially Indonesia, automatic transmission and exports. Management was more cautious on quantifying the automatic transmission and 4WD opportunities, and it framed some revenue targets as conservative. It was defensive when addressing media reports on the Indonesia order.
key_quotes: So our team is in advanced discussions for a technology transfer agreement with a leading global OEM.
It has been won fair and square in a competitive tender that included at least 3 or 4 major Japanese OEMs, and I might add, 2 very large Chinese companies.
The automatic transmission number is extremely conservative.

growth.why: Management expects Transfer Case and Components momentum to continue, backed by Indonesia orders (~70,000 units, on track for FY27), newly secured component programmes nearing INR100 crore annual revenue, and an EV model expected to nearly double volumes from July 2026; EV utilisation is only ~25-30%, and no revenue-level FY27 growth % was given.
